family_history: Mother alive at 84, no cognitive issues

social_history.occupation: Retired chef and restaurant owner; closed restaurant 18 months ago after health department violations and staff complaints
social_history.alcohol: Escalating — husband reports 6 glasses wine daily (previously social only)

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert. Previously creative and organized chef now severely disinhibited. Talks constantly over examiner. MMSE 20/30. FAB 9/18 — severely impaired across all frontal tasks. Category fluency: 6/60 seconds. Bilateral frontal release signs. Severe perseverative behavior observed.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral upper extremity rigidity. 5/5 strength.
neurological_exam.additional: Hyperorality — took and ate a granola bar from examiner's desk mid-exam.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive disinhibition, compulsive eating, and personality change in a 61-year-old chef over 2 years.
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. R. is a 61-year-old left-handed woman referred for evaluation of progressive personality changes over 2 years. Her husband describes her as formerly a meticulous, creative chef who ran a well-regarded restaurant for 15 years. Two years ago, she began making erratic decisions at the restaurant — over-ordering food, screaming at staff in front of customers, and serving meals she had taken bites from. She received multiple health code violations before closing the restaurant 18 months ago. At home, she eats continuously, consuming multiple meals in succession, and has gained 20 lbs. She obsessively rearranges pots and pans in the kitchen in the same pattern repeatedly for hours. She makes offensive remarks to neighbors. She has had several minor car accidents due to impulsive driving. Her wine consumption has escalated from social to 6 glasses daily, which she denies. Husband confirms she shows no distress or insight. No family history of dementia. Thyroid function was checked by PCP and is normal.

findings.location: bilateral frontal lobes, orbitofrontal and dorsolateral

volumetrics.frontal_lobes: 25% below norms — most severe case in series

additional_observations: Preserved posterior parietal and occipital cortex
mri.impression: Very severe bilateral frontal (orbitofrontal and dorsolateral) and moderate-to-severe anterior temporal atrophy with knife-blade gyral pattern. Normal hippocampal volume. Posterior parietal and occipital cortex preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

advanced_imaging.impression: Very severe bilateral frontotemporal hypometabolism — a pattern consistent with a frontotemporal metabolic profile. Posterior cingulate cortex and parietal metabolism preserved. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. Global SUVR 0.90, below positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 125 mmH2O. WBC: 1 cell/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 39 mg/dL. Glucose: 58 mg/dL (ratio 0.66). Abeta42: 870 pg/mL (normal). Total tau: 200 pg/mL (normal). Phospho-tau 181: 34 pg/mL (normal). NfL: 2,490 pg/mL (elevated).

output.impression: Neuropsychological profile consistent with probable behavioral-variant frontotemporal dementia, advanced severity. Very severely impaired executive function (FAB 9/18) and social cognition (Faux Pas 2/20) with moderate retrieval-predominant memory impairment. Very severe disinhibition and hyperorality on caregiver-rated scales. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: Sertraline 50 mg and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime for behavioral symptoms
interactions: Hydrochlorothiazide + sertraline: low interaction; monitor electrolytes
warnings: Combination SSRI + trazodone: low serotonin syndrome risk at low doses; monitor
alternatives: Quetiapine 25 mg for severe agitation only if needed and with specialist input

results.title: Driving in FTD
results.finding: Patients with behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia have markedly elevated crash risk due to impulsivity and judgment impairment; driving safety literature supports cessation even with mild-to-moderate symptom severity

output.summary: Patients with frontal-predominant disinhibition syndromes have markedly elevated driving accident risk due to impulsivity, poor judgment, and disinhibition from orbitofrontal and ventromedial prefrontal dysfunction. Published literature documents significantly elevated crash rates in this population, who should not drive even when global cognitive screening scores are relatively preserved. Clinician reporting requirements for medically at-risk drivers vary by jurisdiction. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

advanced_imaging.impression: No abnormality identified on this advanced imaging study. Findings are non-contributory to the diagnostic question and do not alter management. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), probable, sporadic — advanced stage

differential.key_features: AD with frontal presentation; biomarker testing distinguishes.
Severe progression and imaging confirm neurodegeneration.
No predominant vascular pattern on MRI.
No urinary incontinence; gait disturbance attributable to advanced bvFTD.
No motor neuron signs on exam.

optimal_actions.action: Obtain brain MRI with volumetric coronal T1 to assess frontal/anterior temporal atrophy and exclude alternative structural cause
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bilateral frontal and/or anterior temporal atrophy in a lobar pattern with relative posterior sparing

optimal_actions.action: Order metabolic dementia panel (TSH, B12, CMP, RPR/HIV per risk) to exclude reversible mimics
optimal_actions.expected_finding: No reversible metabolic or infectious cause of cognitive decline identified

optimal_actions.action: Order comprehensive neuropsychological battery characterising executive function, social cognition, language and memory
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Frontal-executive and social-cognition deficits with relative sparing of episodic memory and visuospatial function

optimal_actions.action: Search medical literature for advanced bvftd: behavioural and safety management
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirms Rascovsky 2011 criteria, FDG-PET evidence (Foster 2007), and management approach (Bang 2015)

tool_parameters.query: Advanced bvFTD: behavioural and safety management

optimal_actions.action: Consult behavioral/cognitive neurology for syndromic diagnosis, biomarker interpretation, and longitudinal care plan
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Behavioral neurology confirms bvFTD syndrome, coordinates biomarkers and disclosure

optimal_actions.action: Order FDG-PET brain to characterise frontotemporal hypometabolism and distinguish bvFTD from AD
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Bifrontal and/or anterior temporal hypometabolism with relative posterior sparing
optimal_actions.guideline_source: Foster 2007 FDG-PET in FTD vs AD

optimal_actions.action: Order FTD genetic panel (C9orf72, GRN, MAPT) given negative family history
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identifies or excludes pathogenic C9orf72 / GRN / MAPT variant relevant to prognosis and cascade testing

optimal_actions.action: Discuss symptomatic management (SSRI for compulsive behaviors) and review drug interactions

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
Non-contrast head CT lacks the resolution and lobar specificity needed to characterise frontotemporal atrophy; MRI is the standard structural study.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

sequence_constraints.reason: Exclude structural cause of focal cognitive symptoms and screen for elevated ICP before lumbar puncture.

critical_actions: Address hyperphagia and weight gain with caregiver-mediated dietary control and consider SSRI.
Initiate advanced-care planning, including discussion of long-term care needs and surrogate decision-making.
Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
key_reasoning_points: Advanced bvFTD with prominent hyperorality and compulsive eating; classic Rascovsky features.
Imaging confirms severe lobar atrophy and hypometabolism.
Symptomatic SSRI is reasonable; AChE inhibitors are contraindicated.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild rigidity is common in advanced bvFTD and does not warrant DaTscan.

metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required tools (MRI, labs, neuropsych, literature, consult) plus recommended FDG-PET / amyloid PET / genetic panel; 1–2 red herrings (mild rigidity ± family history); requires cross-modal synthesis (structural + metabolic + biomarker + neuropsych) to exclude AD and document Rascovsky criteria.
